Your order Shop···· is delivered, John. The T. P2 landed November 3, tracking here: (tracking link hidden) The Harlo OS diagnostics add-on went out on the 23rd.

On yesterday's chat, I can't pull the old conversation back up in this window. A copy of each conversation goes to the email on file ((email hidden)) once it closes, so it should be in your inbox, worth checking spam too.

What part of the advice did you need again? I can go over it right here.
Oh, that's disappointing...yesterday's conversation was still ongoing; therefore, was not "closed", and therefore, was not emailed.

Fair point, and sorry about that. I can't reach back into an earlier chat from here, so the fastest fix is this: tell me roughly what we covered, the model or the setup question, and I'll walk through it again properly.

If you'd rather have yesterday's thread itself, I'll ask the team to dig it out and email it to you. Which would you like?

I'll try to remember what I can...I have a Hammer Thor P2; I decided to order a hardware wallet which will arrive in about a week. In the meantime, should I use a Coinbase wallet while I wait for the hardware wallet?

Yes, that works fine. Your pool just needs a payout address, so a Coinbase receive address is a perfectly good placeholder for a week. When the hardware wallet arrives, generate a fresh receive address there and change it in your pool account, nothing on the miner itself changes.

Realistically a week on a Thor P2 won't hit most pools' payout threshold anyway, so the balance will likely still be sitting at the pool when you switch.

Which pool are you on?
How do I find out which pool I am on?

Open the miner's dashboard in a browser, type its IP address into the address bar on the same network. In Harlo OS the Settings or Pool tab shows the stratum URL you're pointed at, something like stratum+tcp://..., plus the worker name. That URL tells you the pool, and the worker name is usually your payout address.

If the dashboard looks different from that, the Harlo OS channel on our Discord is the fastest help: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate (JD).

Can you reach the dashboard?
Yes, is the information in the Stratum Host what you're looking for?

That's the one. The S. Host is the pool, something like public-pool.io, solo.ckpool.org or stratum.braiins.com. Read that line and you know who you're mining with.

Right below it there's usually a Stratum User field. That's your payout address, often with a worker name after a dot. That's the field you'll edit when your hardware wallet arrives.

What does the host line say?
solo.atlaspool.io:3333

That's a solo pool, so you're playing the block lottery, not stacking steady payouts. Nothing accumulates: if your Thor P2 ever solves a block, the reward goes straight to the address in Stratum User. Otherwise nothing arrives.

So the Coinbase address is fine as a stopgap, but swap in the hardware wallet address the day it arrives, since a solo payout lands in one go with no warning.

Want steady small payouts instead? A shared pool would do that, happy to point you at options.
I am actively solo mining on a site called luqee.net and I have a BTC and a BCH address there.  Should I copy and paste one of these here or should I get new payout addresses for the Hammer Miner?

Don't paste them into the chat, just into the miner. And use the BTC one only, never the BCH address on a Bitcoin pool, that money is unrecoverable.

The real question is who holds the keys. If that BTC address is your own wallet's receive address, reusing it is fine. If luqee.net generated it for you, it's their address, not yours, so don't use it on another pool.

When the hardware wallet lands, use a fresh address from it either way.
Do you know how I can check to see if I obtained the payout address from Coinbase or if it was assigned by Luqee?

Easiest check: open Coinbase, go to Bitcoin and tap Receive. Compare that address with the one in the miner. Coinbase rotates receive addresses, so also look under your BTC account's transaction or address history and search for the one you have. If Coinbase shows it, it's yours.

If it doesn't appear anywhere in Coinbase, assume Luqee assigned it and don't reuse it.

Simpler still: just take a fresh Receive address from Coinbase now and use that.
Yes, I did receive the address from Coinbase

Then you're good. Paste that BTC address into the Stratum User field, add a worker name after a dot if you like, for example address.thorp2. Save, let the miner reconnect, and check the dashboard shows accepted shares again within a minute or two.

When the hardware wallet arrives, take a fresh receive address from it and change that same field. Nothing else needs touching.

Anything else on the miner while we're here?
Do I do anything with the password?

No. On nearly every solo pool the stratum password is ignored. Leave whatever is in there, or put x, both work.

The only time it matters is a pool that uses it for difficulty settings, and Atlas doesn't ask for that as far as I know. If the pool's own page says otherwise, follow their page.

So: address in the user field, password left alone, save, watch for accepted shares.
Ok, that worked great!  It's back up and running.  Thank you so much for your help.  Now I am ready to learn more about pools.

Glad it's humming.

Short version: two flavours. Solo, what you're on, means you keep a whole block reward if your miner finds one, and nothing at all otherwise. Lottery odds, huge prize. Shared pools (Braiins, Ocean, Luxor, public-pool for small gear) split every block among everyone by shares, so you get small, steady sats instead.

Same hardware, same hashrate, different payout shape. A Thor P2 at 10 TH/s earns very little either way, so most people run solo for the ticket.

Which way are you leaning?
Is it possible to do 25% solo BTC, 25% solo BCH and 50% pool BCH?

Not on one unit. Harlo OS holds one active pool plus a fallback, and the fallback only kicks in when the first drops. There's no percentage split.

BCH is SHA-256 too, so the Thor P2 can mine either, just not at the same time. Your realistic options are switching the pool manually when you feel like it, or running a second miner on the other chain.

Splitting hashrate properly needs a proxy in front of the miner, which JD on Discord can talk you through: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf
Ok, let's try a BCH pool for a while to see what that generates, please. Also, please define 'sat'.

A sat is a satoshi, the smallest unit of bitcoin: one hundred millionth of a BTC. So 1,000 sats is 0.00001 BTC. People count small mining income in sats because the BTC figures get silly with zeros.

For B., pick a pool that lists a BCH SHA-256 endpoint (ViaBTC and Luxor both do) and copy the host and port straight from their own connection page rather than from me. Then put your BCH address in the user field and save.

Want help reading the result once it's running?
Yes, please...I'll resume this conversation once I have that set up. Thank you.

Sounds good. When you come back, note the pool, your hashrate on the dashboard and the accepted share count, and we'll read it together.

One thing, since yesterday's thread got lost: a copy of this conversation goes to your email once it closes, so you'll have the steps in writing.

Curious, what made you pick solo over a shared pool in the first place, the jackpot or something you read?

I was very happy to help. If you were pleased, a word on Trustpilot means a lot: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/heliumdeploy.com
